title: Ladder Pulls
description:
Ladder pulls are one of CRL's largest architectural hardware categories, but sales fell 13% from 2022 to 2023 as competitors sold similar-looking pulls for close to half the price. Customers didn't understand why ours cost more.

Instead of racing to the bottom, we split the line in two. CRL X is a premium exterior pull in 3 mm, marine-grade 316 stainless for coastal and winter climates, priced against the market's premium brand. CRL I is a 1.5 mm, 304 stainless interior pull at a value price. Both come from a new supplier with a lower cost structure. We focused on the fast-moving sizes, planned a sell-down of the old stock, ran first-article inspections on every component, and took the program through Gate 3.

brief.label: Problem
brief.text: Competitors offered lower-quality pulls at prices close to ours or far below, and customers weren't told why CRL's cost more.

brief.label: Strategy
brief.text: Two lines for two applications: premium exterior and value interior, which limits cannibalization between them.

brief.label: Solution
brief.text: CRL X (316 stainless, 3 mm) for exterior and harsh environments; CRL I (304 stainless, 1.5 mm) for interiors. Both replace the previous line.

brief.label: Customers
brief.text: Architects, temperers, glazing contractors and Division 10 contractors.

brief.label: Market
brief.text: Glass office market over $20B, growing 3.8% a year.

charts.title: Line architecture
charts.caption: Same performance standards, two materials for two environments. 316 stainless resists corrosion far better than 304 thanks to its molybdenum content, which matters in coastal humidity and salted winter air.

quotes.quote: As an owner I am looking for ways to help maximize profit. I must buy ladder pulls from [a low-cost competitor] since they are a significant price difference. I'm not able to justify spending more when I can spend much less for similar results.
